A Sankey (or alluvial) diagram shows how a quantity **flows through a sequence of categorical
stages** — patients moving from a cohort, to a treatment, to an outcome; or reads from a sample, to
a mapping status, to a feature. The width of each stream is the magnitude. Here we build one in R
with [canvasXpress](https://canvasxpress.org) — interactive, and reproducible because the whole
figure is one portable spec.

## The data shape

canvasXpress builds a Sankey from a **tidy table where each row is one path** through the stages,
plus a frequency/weight. Swap this simulated clinical flow for your own counts.

```{r}
#| message: false
library(canvasXpress)

set.seed(1)
cohort <- c(); treat <- c(); outcome <- c(); freq <- c()
for (co in c("Cohort A", "Cohort B"))
 for (tr in c("Drug 1", "Drug 2", "Placebo"))
  for (ou in c("Response", "Stable", "Progression")) {
    base <- if (ou == "Response") 40 else if (ou == "Stable") 25 else 15
    if (tr == "Placebo" && ou == "Response") base <- 12          # placebo responds less
    cohort  <- c(cohort, co); treat <- c(treat, tr); outcome <- c(outcome, ou)
    freq    <- c(freq, base + sample(0:15, 1))
  }
```

The value (`Freq`) is the single measured variable; the stage columns are sample annotations. In
canvasXpress terms: one variable × N path-rows, with the categorical stages as `smpAnnot`.

```{r}
ids <- paste0("r", seq_along(freq))
y <- data.frame(matrix(freq, nrow = 1, dimnames = list("Freq", ids)), check.names = FALSE)
smpAnnot <- data.frame(Cohort = cohort, Treatment = treat, Outcome = outcome,
                       row.names = ids, check.names = FALSE)
```

## The plot

`graphType = "Sankey"` with `sankeyAxes` listing the stages in order, `xAxis` naming the value, and
`colorBy` coloring the streams.

```{r}
canvasXpress(
  data     = y,
  smpAnnot = smpAnnot,
  graphType = "Sankey",
  sankeyAxes = list("Cohort", "Treatment", "Outcome"),
  xAxis      = list("Freq"),
  colorBy    = "Outcome",
  sankeyType = "proportional",
  graphOrientation = "horizontal",
  title = "Patient flow: cohort → treatment → outcome",
  width  = 700,
  height = 500
)
```

Hover any stream to see the count; the widths are proportional to the frequency, so you can read the
flow at a glance — e.g. how much of each cohort ends in Response vs Progression, and how Placebo
differs. `sankeyType` can also be `"aligned"` (classic alluvial) or `"equal"`.

## Why "reproducible"

The `data`+`config` **is** the figure — one portable JSON spec. The same spec renders the identical
Sankey from Python or JavaScript, and can be validated and re-rendered later.
